STORY SO FAR: Mon 08-10, two days to the plane. Short, sharp session on the -laam machine, and it turned into the cleanest demonstration yet of the INVENTORY FINDING working as a teaching METHOD rather than an observation.

THE MACHINE LANDED, IN THREE STEPS. Opened by paying off the morning -laam memo as lore: the tail is a part, not a phrase. He asked the right question himself, unprompted -- '-laam vs -laama?' -- so I gave him the decomposition: -laam proposes, and the -AA on the end is the question tail he ALREADY fires everywhere (irukkaa, saaptingala, theriyumaa). Not a new ending; his own question mark. Then three verbs. (1) Break a post-lunch deadlock: he produced 'market-ku poganum, avasaram irukku' -- correct, cold, unaided, but ANNOUNCING his own business where the family move proposes and pulls the room in. Same shape as venum-for-kudunga; one clause of contrast, no re-teach. (2) He came back 'kilambalaamaa?' -- right, but I had written that exact word two messages above his head, so I logged it HINTED and told him why to his face. Not counting my own scaffolding again. (3) Real ambush, nothing named: half past two, nobody has eaten, everyone standing in the hall. He answered 'kilambalaama' -- the WRONG VERB, carried whole from the previous scene.

NEW SLIP, and it is the productive twin of the inventory finding: chunk-not-machine. He holds the phrase, not the machine, so under pressure he re-uses the whole chunk instead of swapping the slot. One clause of fix (swap the verb at the front -- saapidalaamaa) and then the third verb, cold, nothing from me: UKKARALAAMAA. The machine is running. Teaching by decomposition beat teaching by chunk again, second sitting running.

STRANGER-NGA IS CLOSED. Auto scene at the end -- driver doing forty, her street the next right, nothing in the prompt about endings or politeness. He fired 'medhuva ponga. valadhu pakkam ponga.' -NGA ON BOTH VERBS, unaided, to a stranger: the ending he chronically drops, and the exact 07-27 slip ('medhuva pesa', bare stem) now clean. NOT COUNTED, deliberately: the deck chunk valadhu pakkam thirumbunga -- he produced 'ponga', which a driver would act on, so it is a working substitute, not that item. Do not grade him against the fixed phrasing; do get thirumbunga into his ear.

FIRES: 5 cold (frame:needtogo-place on a novel slot, avasaram irukku, frame:mayi-laama on ukkara, frame:polite-nga twice novel, frame:adverb-aa) + 1 hinted (kilambalaamaa).

M86 SHIPPED MID-SESSION -- 'The Family That Never Decides', 7.2 min, lore/mischief: the -laam tail spoken BARE and bolted onto six verbs before any payload chunk is named, then +aa turns it into a question; the paakkalaam/pakkam pair carved by parts, with his own 'temple pakkalam' error replayed in the third person. That is his airport listening, alongside the three long-haul tapes and M74_v2.

COMMISSIONED: frame:negative-la -- puriyala / mudiyala / theriyala / kekkala. Today's exact shape on a machine he does NOT yet know is a machine: he owns puriyala and mudiyala as separate chunks and has never seen the -la under them. Targets chunk-not-machine directly and finally gives the long-owed puriyala-for-reopen test somewhere to live.

ENGINEERING, SETTLED 08-10 (@build, after the session): the render_audio inline-pause bug is FIXED -- a pause inside a spoken line was eating the line. 56 lines across 13 episodes were never spoken; M74 re-rendered to _v2 and is worth a listen, the other twelve stand ("fail forwards", Andrew's rule). Still red and NOT mine: the chat.md smoke case, almost certainly a Windows CRLF artifact.

STILL OPEN: puriyala-for-reopen (now commissioned). Volley frozen at 2/4. Delight 5 cold of 27; three zinger items never worked. Watch item still at n=1: English-shaped noun where the Tamil wants a verb ('Evlo Rubai?'). TONIGHT'S MISSION: propose ONE thing to her with -laamaa instead of announcing it -- dinner is the guaranteed slot, packing night guarantees a second. ERA TURNS AT TOUCHDOWN: the field mission becomes the session's INPUT, countdown and burn rate drop off the status line, never narrate a deficit in country.

soak_order.scene_seed: an errand where nothing works: the shop is shut, the phone will not connect, nobody can remember the man's name -- every beat is a different verb failing, and the person telling it is enjoying the disaster far too much
soak_order.focus: the -ல negative as ONE MACHINE under chunks he already fires whole. He owns புரியல and முடியல as separate memorised chunks and has never heard the -ல as a part. Make the tail audible across verbs he owns -- புரியல, முடியல, தெரியல, கேட்கல, பண்ணல, வரல -- so the swap is the payload and the words are its output; same treatment the -லாம் tail just got in M86. Also carve புரியல's conversational JOB, not just its shape: it CLOSES the exchange ('I don't understand', give up) where என்ன சொன்னீங்க? REOPENS it -- he owns the giving-up line and not the keep-going line, and that test has been owed for weeks.
